short: Sentence decoding from a person who cannot speak holds for 50 words and one participant; the decoder is standard, and an LM restricted to the test vocabulary drives the gain.
position: The paper changed who is decoded (M04, a participant with anarthria and a chronic implant) and moved a closed-vocabulary pipeline from speaking epilepsy patients into that setting (M06, M07); each component is standard for 2021 ECoG work, and the advance is the population, not the decoder. The main claim, sentences decoded from a person who cannot speak, holds for 50 words and one participant at 25.6% median WER. The strongest overreach is the language model: it was trained only on sentences built from the same 50 words as the test set, so the drop from 60.5% to 25.6% WER measures a closed-world prior. The no-recalibration claim rests on a post hoc offline analysis of isolated words, not on real-time sentence use. Against today the decoder is far behind: 99.6% accuracy on 50 words after 30 minutes of data [@card2024] ([later]), where this paper used 22 hours.
